newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IRISH S/A PRIVATE SECTOR CREDIT GROWTH 20.6PCT Y/Y.
newsitem.headline: IRISH S/A PRIVATE SECTOR CREDIT GROWTH 20.6PCT Y/Y.

text.p: Ireland's adjusted annual private sector credit growth was 20.6 percent at end-June versus 18.9 percent in May, the central bank said on Thursday.
Analysts forecasts ranged from 19 to 20 percent.

"It is estimated that around one percentage point of the increase in the annual adjusted rate of private-sector credit growth was related to subscriptions for shares in the Norwich Union," the central bank said in a statement.
It said tax payments were also likely to have boosted credit growth in June with corporation tax receipts substantially higher than in the same month last year, due largely to timing factors.
The central bank said even allowing for these factors credit growth remained strong with little sign of deceleration in the underlying rate of increase.

Residential mortgage lending was modestly stronger than in earlier months rising to 14.6 percent from 14.4 percent while non-mortgage Irish-pound credit increased at an annual rate of 23.4 percent compared with 21.1 percent the previous month, the central bank said.
